lesson.subject: science
lesson.title: New Life and Growing Up
lesson.summary: Baby animals, how animals and people grow and change, and what animals need to stay alive.
lesson.unit: Topic 7: New life and growing up
learning_objectives: Say that animals have young that grow into adults
Put a life cycle in order
Name what animals need to stay alive

standards.text: Notice that animals, including humans, have offspring which grow into adults; find out about and describe the basic needs of animals, including humans, for survival (water, food and air)

success_criteria: I can name some baby animals
I can put a life cycle in order
I can say what animals need to stay alive
lesson.real_life: Lambs and goats on a farm, hens in a village, and ducklings in a park in spring.

warm_up.prompt: What do we call a baby cat?
warm_up.explanation: A baby cat is a kitten.

blocks.markdown: Today's big question: how do animals grow and change?
blocks.say: Today we meet baby animals. How do animals grow and change?

blocks.alt: A fluffy yellow chick standing in short green grass
blocks.caption: A chick is a young bird. It will grow into a hen or a rooster.
blocks.credit: Photo by Murphy Stay on Unsplash
blocks.say: This chick is only a few days old. It is a baby bird.

blocks.markdown: **Young** animals are baby animals. Many look like a smaller parent.
blocks.say: A baby animal is called a young animal. Many young animals look like their parents.

scenes.caption: Hen and chicks.
scenes.say: A hen has chicks. The chicks look like tiny hens.

scenes.caption: Cow and calf.
scenes.say: A cow has a calf. A calf looks like a small cow.

scenes.caption: Sheep and lamb.
scenes.say: A sheep has a lamb. The lamb stays close to its mother.

question.prompt: Which one of these is a young animal?
question.explanation: A lamb is a baby sheep.

blocks.text: Stop 2: Young animals that look different

blocks.markdown: A **tadpole** looks very different from a frog.
blocks.say: Some babies look very different from their parents. They change a lot as they grow.

scenes.caption: A tadpole.
scenes.say: A tadpole has a tail and no legs. It lives in water.

scenes.caption: A frog.
scenes.say: A frog has legs and no tail. It can live on land.

scenes.caption: Caterpillar and butterfly.
scenes.say: A caterpillar has no wings. A butterfly has big colourful wings.

question.prompt: A tadpole looks just like a grown-up frog.
question.explanation: A tadpole has a tail and no legs. It changes as it grows.

blocks.title: Tara the tadpole
blocks.transcript: I am Tara. I start life as an egg in a pond. I hatch! I have a tail and no legs. I swim. A duckling paddles by. She looks like a small duck. A lamb drinks by the pond. She looks like a small sheep. My back legs grow. I am a froglet now. My tail is gone. I am a frog and I can hop on land. I need food, water, air and shelter, just like you. One day I lay eggs. The life cycle begins again!
blocks.caption: A tadpole tells how she grows into a frog.

points: A tadpole and a caterpillar look very different
blocks.say: Let us remember. Young animals are babies. Some look like their parents. Some look very different.

blocks.markdown: A **life cycle** shows the stages of an animal's life.
blocks.say: A hen lays an egg. A chick grows inside the egg. Then the chick hatches.

scenes.caption: An egg.
scenes.say: First there is an egg. The egg is warm and safe.

scenes.caption: A chick.
scenes.say: The chick hatches. It is small and fluffy.

scenes.caption: A hen.
scenes.say: The chick grows into a hen. She can lay eggs too.

question.prompt: What comes first in a hen's life?
question.explanation: A hen's life begins as an egg.

blocks.alt: A cluster of clear frog eggs with dark centres floating among dry reeds in a pond
blocks.caption: Frogspawn is a mass of frog eggs. Each egg has a tiny tadpole inside.
blocks.credit: Photo by Barnabas Davoti on Unsplash
blocks.say: Frogs lay eggs in water. These eggs are called frogspawn. Tadpoles hatch from them.

scenes.caption: Frog stages.
scenes.say: A frog goes from frogspawn to tadpole to froglet to frog.

scenes.caption: Butterfly stages.
scenes.say: A butterfly goes from egg to caterpillar to chrysalis to butterfly.

scenes.caption: More than two.
scenes.say: Both animals have more than two stages. Many animals do.

blocks.markdown: People **grow** and change through their whole lives.
blocks.say: People have a life cycle too. We start as babies and grow bigger.

blocks.alt: A ewe standing on green grass with two newborn lambs beside her
blocks.caption: A mother sheep with her new lambs. Lambs grow quickly in spring.
blocks.credit: Photo by Nick Fewings on Unsplash
blocks.say: These lambs are only a few days old. Soon they will be bigger and stronger.

scenes.caption: A baby.
scenes.say: A baby needs milk and sleep. Babies grow fast.

scenes.caption: A child.
scenes.say: A child learns, plays and gets taller. Baby teeth fall out.

scenes.caption: An adult.
scenes.say: An adult is fully grown. Adults can work and look after children.

scenes.caption: An older adult.
scenes.say: Older adults change too. Their hair can turn grey.

question.explanation: A child grows into an adult.

blocks.text: Stop 1: Food, water, air and shelter

blocks.markdown: Animals need **food**, water, air and shelter.
blocks.say: All animals need four things to stay alive. They need food and water.

blocks.markdown: Young animals need these things even more.
blocks.say: They also need air to breathe. And they need shelter, a safe place to rest.
Young animals need care from their parents. A lamb drinks its mother's milk.

scenes.caption: Food.
scenes.say: A lamb drinks milk to grow. Later it eats grass.

scenes.caption: Water.
scenes.say: It drinks water from a trough. All animals need water.

scenes.caption: Air and shelter.
scenes.say: It breathes air and sleeps in a barn. That is its shelter.

question.prompt: Pick two things that every animal needs.

blocks.say: A pet cannot look after itself. We must care for it every day.
Muslims are taught to be kind to animals. Giving a pet water is a good deed.

scenes.caption: Water.

scenes.caption: Shelter.
